page_title: Evaluation Metrics for Recommendation Systems - An Overview

summary.title: Evaluation Metrics for Recommendation Systems - An Overview
summary.one_liner: You learn what Recall@K, Precision@K, F1@K, MAP@K, MRR and NDCG measure in recommender systems, with worked movie-list examples, plus a note on popularity bias, position bias and feedback loops.
keywords: how to evaluate a movie recommender
takeaways: Recall@K measures how many of a user's relevant items appear in the top K recommendations; Precision@K measures how many of the K recommendations are relevant.
F1@K is the harmonic mean of precision and recall, so it is high only when both are close to 1.
MAP@K, MRR and NDCG reward relevant items being near the top of the list, with worked examples for each.
NDCG normalizes DCG by the ideal DCG (IDCG) so lists of different sizes can be compared on a 0–1 scale.
Popularity bias, position bias and degenerate feedback loops are important issues to consider when evaluating recommenders.
summary.summary: The article is an overview of common evaluation metrics for recommendation systems, the kind found in ML packages. It defines Recall@K, Precision@K and F1@K with a movie-recommender example where 10 items are recommended. It then covers ranking-aware metrics (Mean Average Precision@K, Mean Reciprocal Rank and NDCG), each explained with small worked examples using lists of movie titles and relevance scores. The closing section briefly describes popularity bias, position bias and degenerate feedback loops, and the author says follow-up articles on these are planned.
